statement.excerpt: To put it bluntly: Cursor's growth story was a lie. It reached $500 million in annualized revenue selling a product it can no longer afford to sell, suggesting material weakness in its own business and any and all coding startups.
statement.document_title: The Hater's Guide To The AI Bubble

from_speaker: Cursor's growth story was a lie
a product it can no longer afford to sell
our_interpretation: The context identifies a June 2025 revenue milestone and changes to the offering before publication on July 21.
Cannot afford means the former offering was economically unsustainable at its existing price and usage terms, rather than that Cursor was insolvent.
Growth story was a lie is read as criticism of the offering's sustainability, not as a separately evidenced allegation that the revenue figure was fabricated.
The industry-wide conclusion is introduced as a suggestion; it is not treated as an independently quantified claim about every startup.
The run-rate figure is treated as a press-reported estimate. ARR terminology must not silently substitute for a disclosed monthly-revenue calculation.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence establishes the stated annualized revenue milestone and shows that the former offering's actual serving costs made its continued sale economically unsustainable.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Matching records disprove the revenue milestone or show that the former offering could sustainably cover its relevant costs. Funding or subsequent growth alone does not establish affordability.
